pattern.crimePattern: daughter-in-law gives the family patriarch an insulin overdose to stop him reporting her husband's theft
pattern.notes: Fictional family, firm, club and "smart" pen. No dosing method is described beyond "dialled up to 60 units", which the pen's own memory reports; no instructions. The family is written as a sad, ordinary family, not as a stereotype.

ob.text: The family of Kisumu businessman Harshad Pandya (68) reports him found dead in bed at 07:30 on Christmas morning at the family home in Milimani. The family doctor, called first, suspects a diabetic emergency.

people.name: Harshad Pandya
people.bio: Third generation in Kisumu. Type 2 diabetic on insulin, and proud of the gadget pen that remembers every dose.

facts.text: Harshad Pandya was found dead in bed at 07:30 on Christmas morning. The family doctor suspects a diabetic emergency.
He lies on his back in bed. No sign of a struggle. A half-drunk glass of water on the bedside table.
The pen's dose memory: 24 December, 22:45 — 14 units. 24 December, 23:41 — 60 units.
Harshad's diary, in his hand: "24 Dec, 22:45, 14 u, abdomen." Every entry for three years says abdomen. Nothing after 22:45.
Sabina: "Bapuji never let anyone touch his pen. Not his wife when she was alive, not me, not the doctor. He was proud of it."
Sabina: Priya took Bapuji a glass of water every night at about half past eleven.
Sabina: at 23:36 she heard the stair creak and a water glass clink past her door, going up to Bapuji's room. "Priya, with his water."
Sabina was in her room off the kitchen from 23:00; she sleeps downstairs.
Sabina: Ernest went to the staff quarters at 22:50. The yard gate's chain was still on in the morning.
Ernest: on the drive to the club, "Mzee shouted at Rahul about money. He said, 'the twenty-seventh, police'. Madam Priya was sitting in the middle row."
Harshad's red-pen circles: KSh 9.2 million transferred over two years to an account controlled by Rahul. A sticky note: "Auditors 27th."
Harshad's will divides the estate among the family, and a share transfer last year already gave Rahul 60% of the firm.
Club bill: the Pandya family's table closed and they left at 22:30.
Club steward: Anil Mehta left at 22:40 with his own driver, for Riat Hills.
Club steward: raised voices between the Pandya table and Anil Mehta's at about 21:30.
Wycliffe: Anil was home in Riat Hills by 23:05, and had eight guests until 01:00.
Priya's fitness app: steps logged from 23:37 to 23:46 with a raised heart rate. Otherwise still from 23:05 to 06:50.
Sabina, Rahul and Ernest give their fingerprints voluntarily.
Fingerprints taken from Priya Pandya in detention.
Autopsy: severe hypoglycaemia, with very low glucose in the eye fluid.
Autopsy: two recent injection sites, one in the abdomen and one in the right thigh.
Autopsy: death between 01:30 and 04:00.
Autopsy: no heart attack, no signs of smothering or of any struggle.
Toxicology: insulin far above any treatment dose. Nothing else in his blood but a glass of wine.
Lab: Harshad's prints on the pen's barrel. Priya's prints on the dose dial. Nobody else's.
Priya: "I went to bed at eleven and didn't leave our room until morning."
Priya refuses to hand over her phone. "My phone is private."
Priya admits she took Harshad his water that night, "as I always do".
Priya: "He was asleep. I put the glass down and came back. I never touched his pen."
Rahul: "Priya was beside me all night."
Rahul: he stayed in bed. Priya got up; he doesn't know for how long. He admits taking the money from the firm.
Anil: "I left at twenty to eleven and had guests at home."
Anil: "I offered to buy. He refused. Old men refuse."
Ernest: "I went to my quarters at ten to eleven."
Ernest: his wages and his Christmas bonus were paid on the 20th. "Mzee never paid late."
Sabina: there has been no quarrel about the grandchildren's school. "They agreed on that school two years ago."

interrogations.intro: Priya sits at the dining table with her hands around a cup she isn't drinking. "I went to bed at eleven. I didn't leave our room until morning."

topics.reply: He never let anyone touch it. Everyone knows that. ...No, you can't have my phone. My phone is private.

interrogations.intro: Rahul paces the veranda under the Christmas lights. "Priya was beside me all night. Please, my father is dead, why are you asking about my wife?"

topics.reply: That is a business matter. I would rather discuss it with a lawyer.

interrogations.intro: Anil receives you in his garden with a cup of coffee. "Tragic. We were rivals for thirty years. That is not the same as enemies."

topics.reply: I offered to buy. He refused. Old men refuse. My driver took me home; ask him. Eight people were in this garden until one.

interrogations.intro: Ernest stands by the car with his cap in his hands. "I drove them home at half past ten. I went to my quarters at ten to eleven."

topics.reply: Mzee never paid late. My wages and the Christmas money came on the twentieth. Take my fingerprints if you want; take everyone's.

interrogations.intro: Sabina has set the Christmas lunch table anyway, one chair pushed in. "Bapuji never let anyone touch his pen."

topics.reply: I don't know about money. I know there has been no fighting about the children's school, if that's what they tell you. That was settled two years ago.

interrogations.intro: Tom Were spikes another bill. "Table 4 left at half ten. Mr Mehta's table, ten minutes after. There were voices earlier."

contradictions.reaction: Rahul sits down on the veranda step. "...She got up. I don't know for how long. I didn't ask. Please. It was my fault, the money, all of it."
"...I took him his water, as I always do. He was asleep. I came back."
Priya looks at the print photograph of the dose dial for a long time. "He was going to put my husband in prison on the twenty-seventh. My children's father." Then nothing.

events.why: The club bill closes table 4 at 22:30.
14 units at 22:45, in the pen's memory and in his own diary: abdomen, as always.
The pen remembers 60 units at 23:41, inside the nine minutes Priya's phone was walking; the thigh site is one he never used.
Severe low blood sugar, hours after the dose: between 01:30 and 04:00.

decoys.why: 07:30 is when he was found on Christmas morning.

prosecutor.pass: Home at half ten, his own dose at quarter to eleven, sixty units at 23:41, dead before dawn. The pen kept better time than the family.
fail: Half past seven is when they found him.
There are two doses in that pen's memory. Which one was his?

prosecutor.pass: Up and walking from 23:37 to 23:46, the only one who ever went to his room at that hour, and her prints on the dial. That will hold.
fail: Rahul lied for her; he never left the bed. Whose prints are on the dial?
Mr Mehta had eight guests in his garden. Look inside the house.

prosecutor.pass: Sixty units, in a thigh he never used, from his own pen. Yes.
fail: It looks natural. Read the pen's memory.
Nothing in his blood but insulin and a glass of wine.

prosecutor.pass: "The twenty-seventh, police." She was in the middle row. That's the reason. And Rahul answers for the nine million.
fail: Rahul already holds sixty per cent. Nothing changes for her.
Mr Mehta's offer was refused at the club. That's his matter.

timeOfDeath.note: The act window: the 60-unit dose at 23:41, between the stair creak at 23:36 and the end of Priya's steps at 23:46. He died of it between 01:30 and 04:00.

proof.concludes: After his normal 14 units at 22:45, in the abdomen as always, someone gave him 60 units at 23:41, in the thigh, a site he never used. He died of severe low blood sugar hours later.
Harshad never let anyone touch his pen. The only person who came to his room at that hour, every night, was Priya with his water; Sabina heard her on the stairs at 23:36.

Priya didn't stay in bed and Rahul didn't know where she was: her phone walked from 23:37 to 23:46, and she admits taking the water up. Home at 22:30, his dose at 22:45, 60 units at 23:41, dead by 04:00.

Her prints are on the dose dial. On the way to dinner she heard Harshad tell Rahul "the twenty-seventh, police" over the money he'd taken. Priya Pandya killed Harshad with a deliberate overdose of his own insulin, to stop him reporting her husband's theft.

eliminations.why: Rahul stayed in bed while Priya got up, and his prints are not on the pen. His crimes are the theft and the lie.
Anil was home in Riat Hills by 23:05 with eight guests until 01:00.
Ernest went to the staff quarters at 22:50, and the yard gate stayed chained until morning.
Sabina was in her room off the kitchen; she heard Priya pass at 23:36. Her prints are not on the pen.
A 60-unit dose at 23:41, in the thigh, and insulin far above any treatment dose.
Nothing in his blood but insulin and a glass of wine.
No heart attack; he died of low blood sugar.
No signs of smothering or of any struggle.
Rahul already holds 60% of the firm; nothing changes for Priya.
That offer is Anil's, refused at the club, and Anil was at home with guests.
There was no such quarrel; the school was agreed two years ago.
Ernest's wages and bonus were paid on the 20th, and that was never Priya's matter.

reconstruction.text: Over two years Rahul moves KSh 9.2 million out of the family firm to cover a failed investment. On Christmas Eve afternoon Harshad finds it in the accounts.
In the car to the club he tells his son: "On the twenty-seventh, the auditors and the police." Priya, in the middle row, hears it.
22:30, home. 22:45, his usual 14 units, written in his diary: abdomen. He goes to sleep.
23:36. Priya climbs the stairs with his glass of water, as every night. At 23:41 she dials his pen to 60 units and injects him in the thigh.
She goes back to bed. Rahul feels her come back and asks nothing. Harshad dies in the early hours. At Christmas lunch, Sabina leaves his chair pushed in.

clockPlan.note: One warrant on Priya's phone. Detain her once she admits taking the water up; her prints are taken in detention and the dial result (6 h) breaks her second story inside the 24 hours.

ui.beatNotes: Devices that remember. The pen's dose memory and the phone's step log are read as timelines and dropped straight onto the rail. Both are clocks nobody thought of as witnesses.
